jm_die_training_data_policy.SEVERITY: CRITICAL — MUST be enforced before any S7 ingestion unit executes
jm_die_training_data_policy.authoritative_statement: JM Die Company's 24,545 archived programs are REAL-WORLD SHOP PROGRAMS THAT RAN AND PRODUCED PARTS. They are NOT optimized. They represent: (a) what a skilled human programmer using Mastercam X8 / Fusion 360 / Inventor HSM / hyperMILL / Okuma IGF chose as *good enough to ship* under that shop's real constraints (tool availability, fixturing, quoted cycle time, operator skill, controller version). They are the empirical baseline PRISM must UNDERSTAND as ground-truth-on-what-ran, and then BEAT in measurable terms (cycle time, tool life, Ra, cost). They are NOT the target the AI should maximize toward.

ml_training_policy.loss_function_treatment: JMDie programs enter training as STATE-OUTCOME pairs (input_context → what-the-shop-actually-chose) with BEAT-THE-SHOP objective — the optimization target is a function of (physics-predicted optimum − shop's actual choice), not shop's-actual-choice itself
ml_training_policy.reward_shaping: Reward = improvement over JMDie baseline on (cycle time, tool life, MRR, Ra) subject to constraints (same tooling crib, same fixture class, same machine). Matching or underperforming JMDie on all metrics = zero reward, not positive.
ml_training_policy.label_class_requirement: Every JMDie-sourced training row carries `label_class: 'empirical_not_optimal'`. Training splits MUST stratify on this to avoid the model learning 'JMDie's answer is correct' as a prior.
ml_training_policy.comparison_benchmark_requirement: Any S&F or strategy recommendation engine that trains on JMDie data MUST publish a 'vs-JMDie-delta' metric alongside absolute output, reported in quote outputs + physics explanations.
